descending into the career intern life lol', 'incident during synth lab lecture hi everyone, most of y\'all might not have known what happened yesterday, so heres the story for context: a group of four or five guys that were not part of a lecture were sitting in the back of the lecture hall, and during the session, one of the guys was being obnoxious when the professor was trying to teach the class, like answering in class questions by shouting out jokes like "lebron james" and "21," and being overall disruptive to the class. the professor asked him to stop but he wouldn\'t, so he got frustrated and angry, and asked the student to leave. he tried to stay in the class by remaining in his seat, and tried to say sorry and said "i thought the joke was funny" but the professor was silent and was not going to continue the lecture until the guy had left. the guy was stalling the class, slowly walking his way out, he even tried to sit in the back corner of the lecture hall to try and wait for the professor to give in and let him stay. he slowly walked down the stairs, and some people in the class were telling him to leave because he kept trying to stall and delay the class, and he shouted "f u" to them and left. for the next five minutes, he kept staring through the small glass of the window, and then he eventually walked back in with two soda beverages trying to apologize to the professor, asking him to accept them and let him back into the class. the professor said no and asked him to leave, but he still tried to get him to accept the drinks. the professor then said that he will call gtpd if he does not leave. he put the drinks down on the podium and walked towards the door, but he did not go through it and was hiding behind a blind spot of where the door is. he then tried to peer over behind a wall to see if we noticed him. at that moment one of the guys walked down towards him, grabbed him, and shoved and dragged the guy out the door with him. the other remaining guys walked their way out through the door, and none of them returned to the class after that. since physical confrontation was present at that point, the professor had to call gtpd to file a report, and class was dismissed early once the police arrived. and during all of this, my friends and i were scared and anxious, not knowing what was going to happen next, because we didn\'t know if it was all fake or not. we were worried that when the guy left the first time, that he could come back in with a weapon. i\'m so grateful that that was not the case, but it does not dismiss the fact that i\'m angry about this. people were scared, they had adrenaline kick in, and some were scared of walking back home. the strange thing is that even the person that shoved him out of the lecture hall was apparently also not part of the class. the question now is if they were even tech students. i\'m starting to think that it might be staged, which makes me even more mad. assuming that this was staged, why would you pull such a stupid prank or joke like that. the only thing that they accomplished yesterday was put fear in people. all for what? gaining attention? views? i didnt see any one of them recording but if they did i hope they realize how stupid they look. even if it was not staged, it still falls on the guy who was being disrespectful. this is supposed to be a lecture, and i get that there can be a few jokes in class that might be more class related, but otherwise it is a serious learning environment. this guy was not obeying that, and was just outright being rude and disruptive. the professor asked him to stop multiple times and he still continued on with being obnoxious. people are trying to learn, and you\'re taking that away from them. you\'re just being a detriment to the school, whether you are an actual student here or not. on a side note, i\'ll be honest, i am one of those people that complain about social media like tik tok and how its poisoning the minds of our generation even if to some people that might sound like an exaggeration, but honestly there\'s without a doubt that certain content on there promotes this sort of behavior, and even the defenders of social media cannot deny that this is a terrible outcome of it. im sure that the people on reddit are not prone to having this sort of behavior, but i really hope that anyone reading this does not mimic what happened yesterday. it\'s really not funny, in fact its actually infuriating to think about. you not only disrupt the class and prevent students from learning about their course and future assignments, you also put people in fear and distress. you only hurt yourself when you do something like this. please think twice before you do this sort of thing, and ask yourself what could the outcome be. you might find yourself in a better position by shutting your mouth up and moving on rather than opening it and eventually getting your ass handed to you. edit: update: thank you all for the comments, makes me feel better about the situation. anyways here is the update. the individuals were identified and its confirmed that they aren\'t enrolled at tech, nor are they from in-state. they traveled to atlanta from out of state for some convention and had time before their return trip so that was when they decided to come to campus to do the pranks. its also confirmed that they also went to other classrooms to do the same thing, which confirms the other cases some of y\'all mentioned in the comments. charges are being pursued with the intention of warning them to not do this sort of thing again. kinda do feel bad about them being pressed charges, but with there being five of them plus the teacher making it clear to stop, and they also did it in other lectures, from a perspective i think it is deserved. still, makes part of me hope the charges are not as severe and that really in the end they just learn their lesson and not do it again. especially during this time with all the violence and political drama, this sort of prank is just not worth doing since it has the potential to do damage. i understand that theres a time for being funny, and that this sort of thing might have be more acceptable and maybe funny in a different time period, but the timing was not good at all, and that they should have thought about it twice instead of making the situation into a headache for all of us.']

Representative_Docs: ['ngl, you cs have it so good, you have no idea. as for the comment about making 250k, go and google “average salary of person (insert your age)” then do the same thing adding ten years. you are likely at the top 1% of people your age. if you are unhappy with being in the top 1% and don’t think you can be making 250k in 10-15 yrs as a swe, i doubt anything you do will make you happy. also, who gives a fuck give a fuck what your parents or whoever think? as for the second part, many doctors go out and work for a decade before deciding it’s not for them. it’s changed a bit and gotten more selective, but i don’t think it’s ever too late, as long as you are willing to demonstrate an interest by working in medical field doing low level medical jobs or volunteering and killing the mcat (source: my sister is premed rn, so basing this off what she said). however, you mention wanting to make a difference as a reason for switching… doctors are extremely unhappy!!! they have some of the highest rates of burnout and suicide of anyone, unless you are strongly passionate about medicine, you won’t enjoy it! that’s not to mention the fact you will likely have to go hundreds of thousands deeper into debt to get a medical degree, and the entire time you will not be making any money. compound interest is a thing of beauty, you can look at exponential growth models online, but you’re smart enough as a tech student, i shouldn’t have to explain that to you… what makes you so sure you will hate working? i assume you had some swe internships so you know what the work is like, but work is very different from school, almost everyone i know likes work far better than school, so if you haven’t done an internship or smtg i’d give it a shake. idk man, the question seems real to you, but tbh it comes off as kinda whiny. most people would kill for a swe job rn and would be happy making any amount of money doing it', 'but i’m still a student 💔', "as an ex-double major, i think it's not worth doing a double major unless there's a very specific particular thing you want to do that requires such an education. i also thought about doing a minor, but eventually found it easier to just take the handful of additional classes without having to worry about a minor. not doing 2 full curriculums also allows you time outside of classes for hands-on experience via research, clubs, etc. as for logistics, cs is being more restrictive in terms of switching into the major. i am unaware of the exact rules and whether it's different for adding a major, but i'm not sure this is possible if you didn't apply to cs and get in from that."]

Name: 1_campus_housing_parking_atlanta
Representative_Docs: ["ferst dr. - 6th st. intersection rework just wanted to a have a discussion about the feasibility of making the ferst. dr. - 6th st. intersection -- the intersection down the hill from the crc, nearby the west residence halls, the burger bowl, the love building, etc. -- both safer and more efficient at reducing traffic for all: drivers, bikers/scooters, and pedestrians. the current infrastructure for this intersection has pretty large signs on each side of the intersection that flash when a pedestrian or light vehicle presses a button, warning the drivers. as these signs don't actually moderate flow like stop signs or lights, they just warn, there are also stop signs. however the characteristics of this intersection create an interesting right-of-way pattern: you can't call it a 4-way stop, even though it has 4 perpendicular directions of motion for each mode of transportation. to the driver, it's a 2-way, there's only going straight, or turning west; its not a 3-way since 6th street here is one-way; it's not a 4-way since cars can't travel east onto the sidewalk that leads to boggs and on to the culc. to the light vehicle (again, bikes and scooters), its legally a 4-way -- east towards culc, north, south towards crc, and west towards the residence halls, each direction having stop signs. but only as of recently have these stop signs actually been obeyed, as countless times i witness (and i'm guilty as well a few times), light vehicles just blasting through the stop signs. i have seen a reddit post somewhere on this subreddit from gtpd saying they were going to crackdown on this disobeying. i have seen on multiple occasions a cop car sitting on the sidewalk waiting to spot someone. to the pedestrian, the stop sign isn't present, as the pedestrian (unless there's a walk/no walk sign) always has the right of way at intersections ​ just from observing the intersection at rush hour, its just obviously inefficient. what i witness is a car staying at a stop sign for 20 or 30 seconds or more because as the car rolls up to the stop sign, a pedestrian from the right side starts to cross . . . then as p#1 is almost done crossing, p#2 from the left starts to cross . . . then a bike from the right goes right through the stop sign . . . and then the road is clear to continue. this amount of time compounds greatly during rush hour to create a line of cars that sometimes goes up to the crc. do i have a definitive solution? no, for multiple reasons, not being an expert in city planning being one of them. do i have an idea or suggestion that i feel like could be discussed. yes! thats why i made this post :) those who frequent the bioengineering center or the nanotechnology center know that at the intersection between atlantic dr. nw and ferst dr. has a light, but not only does it have a light for cars, but also a light for bicycles. having a light between the light vehicles/pedestrians and the cars would coordinate the motion between the two groups, thereby improving the speed and safety of each. ​ what do you guys think? could something similar be implemented at 6th street? for economic reasons should it be? is it even needed in the first place or is the intersection fine as it is?", 'i am not enjoying east campus and really just missing west. i’m currently a third year here and for the past 2 years i have lived on west campus. i got housing last minute in late july so there was hardly a chance to swap rooms, to go to another dorm. i just really miss the peacefulness of west and how quite the surroundings were. majority of people on east are party people, which i am definitely not. and in 2 of my summers that i have spent on campus, i lived on east, and it wasn’t that bad. i acknowledge though there are a lot less people and activity in the summer. i just wish i could move back to west campus, whether in student dorms or off-campus. i’m heavily considering canceling my housing next semester and just being a commuter (i live an hour away). i know some people may think it’s not that serious but going back to my dorm everyday just bums me out and i feel so much more depressed in the east environment.', 'tl;dr: if you want to get the most out of your tech experience, i\'d encourage living within walking/biking distance of campus. i tried living at my folks\' atp home sophomore year and ended up moving to home park midway through. we weren\'t even as far away as you; 3 minutes to spaghetti junction and maybe 20 to my tech parking deck without traffic. the three things that killed my commuter experience: lack of participation in unscheduled social activities. so much of the college experience is the impromptu group study session, late night playing \\[board/card/video\\] games, or just getting a burger and beer with friends. once i was back home after classes, i never felt like driving all the way back to campus (often at rush hour) just to hang out for an hour or two. weekends were often a total loss. spending countless hours just waiting around for the next class/lab/activity. maybe you\'ll have good luck with scheduling but sometimes you\'re stuck with a 9am class, a 3pm class, and then a 6pm study session. driving back and forth felt like a waste of time so i\'d just sit around the coc or library. i rationalized it by saying "i\'ll study and do homework!" but it\'s so draining to do this multiple times per week. just sitting in traffic for an hour or more per day. sure, the drive was 20 minutes without traffic-- but even back in 2004 atlanta traffic was terrible and the commute would often be 45+ minutes. marta would have taken even longer between driving to doraville or chamblee station, parking, waiting on the train (marta service isn\'t frequent), getting to 10th st or north ave, and then walking to class. this is to say nothing of some common extracurricular activities after which you might not want to drive or might benefit from a room to yourself near campus. i totally get trying to save money. i tried it myself. but moving back near campus was worth the expense for me. eta: i was in a similar financial situation where i was on hope and my folks weren\'t paying for housing. so when i say "worth the expense", it was a direct financial consideration on my part.']

Name: 6_time_just_like_help
Representative_Docs: ['care and mental health services at gt?', 'petition to provide mental health services to disabled gt students right now, georgia tech students in the excel program (students with intellectual or developmental disabilities) do not have access to the georgia tech center for mental health care and resources nor do they have any affordable mental health resources available to them within their program. these students pay tuition and deserve mental health care just like every other student. we want to convince the staff / diversity office to create a mental health program for students within the excel program, starting with a certified therapist or access to the center for mental health care and resources for these students. please sign this to show your support! we will be using this petition when we present our case. your name and electronic signature will not be shared with anyone or used for any other cause and will be discarded afterwards. [', "i have struggled with anxiety and depression for as long as i've been in tech. the best thing to do is seek mental help as soon as possible. everything will be okay. :) i sought help and i'm doing a lot better than before. if you want someone to speak with directly, i don't mind helping you through the process. i understand that it can be scary to navigate through all this. i recommend visiting care and getting a list of therapists and psychiatrists in network with your insurance, off-campus. getting an on campus appointment is really hard. if care is being slow, contacting your insurance provider and asking them for a list can help you get some names. the hardest part is getting the first appointment--try to call everyone you can, give them a brief summary of what you are dealing with, and get their earliest available appointment. a therapist can help break down whatever you are dealing with and directly address the issue. a psychiatrist can help prescribe medication for the same. i am the kind of person who is paralyzed by anxiety and has zero motivation. having a rigid calendar, a to-do list with every little thing i need to do, and a journal to write down what i'm feeling when anxious really helped me cope and stay on top of work. daily meditation and breathing techniques can help too. a muscle relaxation exercise is a great way to refresh your brain when you feel stuck in an infinite loop of intrusive thoughts. but the important thing is to keep trying and not give up on yourself. we are only three weeks away from the end of the semester. you've come this far, you should be proud of yourself!! you can make it to the finish line. :) ​ anxiety can be really hard to deal with when intrusive thoughts set in or you are in an anxious spiral. sometimes the only way to deal with it is to let it flow through you. fighting it doesn't help all the time but accepting that you are anxious and this shall pass can. the techniques i mentioned above may not help all the time but they can reduce the severity of the anxiety you are dealing with. not everyone understands what anxiety feels like, so don't feel disheartened if your close and loved ones are not understanding or kind to you about the situation. this is why i recommend seeking a therapist because you can be as open as you'd like with them. if there is any way your friends can help, let them know what they can do. try to put things into perspective. in a week, if you fail a test, it would most likely matter to you. in a month, maybe less so. how about in a semester, a year, five years, or ten years down the line? your grades are not everything. there is a lot more to you. it is not your fault if you haven't done as well as you would have liked. the unnecessary pressure of needing to be the best can be really depressing when dealing with peak anxiety. your scores will improve as your mental health improves. prioritize your well being. if you have not done so already, contact the dean of students and let them know what you are going through -- they can help ease your academic load and provide any other academic assistance. talk to your professors and tas about it if you can!"]

Name: 8_people_speech_just_say
Representative_Docs: ['advice for a transfer student? i (19 male-to-female) am a 2nd year transfer student at georgia tech, and i\'ve had a shit experience within my first month here. i am aware that there were a few posts in the past talking about this matter, but they all either seem outdated or the general response is just "gatech students are too busy stressing over work to be assholes". this was a relief to hear, until i got on campus. when i had to explain i was trans to someone on the first day of classes after he kept misgendering me, he responded with "oh but you look nothing like a female". i know one other trans friend who\'s told me she\'d been openly mocked for wearing female clothing on campus, and honestly since then it killed my motivation to present as female and has made me depressed. i\'ve literally stopped taking my hormones because i feel so fucking out of place, and i get \'death stares\' each time i tried wearing the clothes i usually wore at my old uni. i get that atlanta is supposed to be a "blue island in a sea of redneck bible-worshippers" but i don\'t see it at all. i\'ve obviously also met supportive people but it seems that the average student here is just not that well informed on these matters. i understand to some extent. i am aware this is a tech school, not a liberal arts college. but those who purposefully go out of their way to make people like me feel like shit have no excuse. and no, it is not just the students. stamps themselves also seem really dense. they literally asked me for my preferred name and pronouns on a form and continued to deadname me and call me sir every time i\'ve went there for anything, as if to make me feel as shitty as possible. at this point i gave up and not even a week in did i stop correcting people for getting my name and pronouns wrong. is this how a fellow yellow jacket is supposed to feel? what\'s the line between mocking and a title ix discrimination case? i literally have no clue what i\'m supposed to do from this point forwards. i will be very grateful for anyone that can give me any advice, trans or not, to make my experience here not miserable :) edit: thank you everyone for the outpouring of advice and support!! this made my day so much better and i\'m feeling more confident now :)) i hope this also helps anyone else who may be transgender!', "public universities need to be a haven to free speech. they are, that's exactly what is happening here. it amazes me when people from any perspective see/hear that someone they disagree with is coming to a place (especially a public university) and they get all enraged. yes, being mad at other peoples speech and voicing it is...as others have noted...free speech. but the labeling of opponents as 'emotional' is still a fun trope to try and distract with. you aren't advocating for free speech, you are fetishizing right wing victim culture. some people have decided they don't need to be open minded to blatant, and moronic, attempts at dehumanization and bigotry. the first amendment is not a toy for right wing victim culture. free speech doesn't mean you get a platform, it doesn't mean you don't hear opposition. it means the state can't impede your speech. i don't think you are a bad guy - i do think i see far to many people buying into bad faith arguments like this. [more fundamentally, if 'its not illegal to say this' is the best argument in favor of some speech - maybe the learned students of georgia tech should strive for information that is higher quality]( it's telling that no one has suggested gt ban her speech, only that everyone is sick of her shit, and you jumped to here.", 'ccf discriminates against lgbt people i loved ccf (christian campus fellowship) when i was at tech, the interns and other students were great, but unfortunately in 2021 the full time staff and board members adopted a policy that bans lgbt people from leadership - they refuse to share the exact wording, but it seems to say that anyone who is in a same-sex relationship may not be an intern or employee at ccf, while it\'s fine to be in a heterosexual relationship. just wanted to share because they are doing their best to hide it and i know what it\'s like to be lured into and invest time in an organization that does not fully accept you. edit: lots of good discussion, stories, clarifications in the comments, i\'d recommend reading through if you\'re just now finding this post. edit 10/26/23: copying my reply from below: sounds like we had just about exactly the same story. my experiences with the other students and interns at ccf about a decade ago did get me out my god-hating anti-theist phase, which largely happened due to the way i saw christians responding to lgbt issues at our evangelical church in high school, and unlike so many other stories i\'ve since read and heard i didn\'t personally have a single negative encounter with anyone at ccf. so it was heartbreaking to learn years later that any affirmation or even love i felt from the staff was not genuine, and to see them continue to harm students today and then to go make themselves out to be the victims when anyone criticizes them (last year the ccf board chairman complained about how the staff were feeling hurt by all the advocacy against their own policy from alumni and students). the harmful part is not the "sexual ethic" as they like to call it, but the employment discrimination policy, and intentional obfuscation of that policy.']

Representative_Docs: ["title: a tale of murky air and unforeseen consequences once upon a time, in a bustling college town, two young friends named alex and ryan shared a small, cozy dorm room. they were college roommates who embarked on an exciting journey of higher education together. little did they know that a seemingly harmless activity could have dire consequences. as the semester went by, alex discovered a passion for cooking. every evening, delicious aromas would waft from their shared kitchenette, as alex whipped up mouth-watering meals for the two of them. however, unseen to the naked eye, minute particles known as pm10 began to silently disrupt their lives. pm10, also known as particulate matter 10, refers to tiny airborne particles with a diameter of 10 micrometers or less. these particles can be released into the air through various sources, including cooking, burning fuels, or even outdoor pollution. unfortunately, the kitchen ventilation system in the student housing was outdated, unable to effectively filter out these harmful particles. slowly but surely, the pm10 particles began to accumulate in their dorm room. ryan, who spent most of his time studying and seldom cooked, began to experience an unexplained decline in his health. persistent coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath crept into his life, making it more difficult for him to focus on academics or enjoy his college experience. initially, ryan dismissed his symptoms as merely common college stress. however, the symptoms persisted and started to affect his daily life. concerned, ryan sought medical advice. after a battery of tests and consultations, the doctors were puzzled by his worsening condition. little did anyone suspect that the invisible culprit lay in the air they breathed. meanwhile, alex remained unscathed, unaware of the danger lurking in the air they shared. since they were not aware of the potential risks, they continued their daily routine. the cooking sessions continued, with pm10 particles floating invisibly in the air, particularly during the more intense cooking moments. as time went on, ryan's health further deteriorated. doctors eventually discovered a link between his exposure to pm10 particles and the development of a serious respiratory illness. the relentless onslaught of these hazardous particles had taken a toll on his body, compromising his immune system and leaving him vulnerable to greater harm. the news was devastating for both ryan and alex. alex blamed themselves for unknowingly subjecting their friend to these hazards, never realizing the consequences of their cooking activities. together, they embarked on a mission to raise awareness about indoor air pollution, especially among their fellow students. alex and ryan became advocates for improved ventilation systems in college dormitories, hoping to protect other students from suffering a similar fate. their story reached the media, and their voices were heard by policymakers and administrators. the college took action, implementing updated ventilation systems, and launching awareness campaigns about the importance of clean indoor air. tragically, ryan's condition worsened despite their best efforts. he fought valiantly, embracing his role as an advocate for clean air in college settings, but ultimately succumbed to his illness. however, his legacy lived on, echoing through the halls of their once-shared dorm room and inspiring others to take action. in memory of their lost friend, alex continued to champion the cause, working alongside health professionals and environmental activists to promote clean indoor air policies on university campuses nationwide. although they carried the weight of grief, they found solace in knowing that their efforts would spare other roommates from similar harrowing experiences. in the end, this tragic story emphasized the importance of recognizing the potential dangers of indoor air pollution. it highlighted the need for continuous improvement in air quality, ensuring that college students, and indeed all people, can breathe freely and live healthy lives.", 'i expect living in gt housing to reduce your life expectancy by a marginal 1 month (and what to do about it) i recently read a [blog post]( which relied on (what looks to me like) [fairly robust research]( (see [also]( to point out that air pollution is a huge health factor that\'s fairly easy to address and seems to be systematically underleveraged (presumably because people don\'t know about it). there\'s a strong and approximately linear relationship between exposure to particulate matter measuring 2.5 microns in diameter or less (pm2.5, measured in ug/m\\^3) and the amount of time you lose from your life as a result. some small amount of indoor air pollution is inevitable - we live in the middle of a particularly car-heavy city, and if people are (reasonably) opening their windows to get fresh air, there will be some nonzero steady-state concentration of particulate matter. the [who gives]( an air quality guideline level of 5 ug/m\\^3, and the outdoor air in atlanta is usually at something like 12 ug/m\\^3 - but this isn\'t terrible. my (off-campus) apartment has a reasonably good hvac system, even though the filter hasn\'t been changed for at least 16 months, and until i bought an air filter, the pm2.5 level was 8 ug/m\\^3, which is pretty ok. i know this because i bought a pm2.5 sensor. unfortunately for those of you living in gt housing, i took that sensor to a friend\'s dorm room and measured pm2.5 levels there at more than 100 ug/m\\^3. we can use the linear relationship described earlier between lifespan (which the 2017 study converts to dalys, disability-adjusted life-years, to account for the fact that among the risks of exposure to pollution are diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and chronic respiratory diseases, all of which will not only shorten your life but may result in disability) and pm2.5 levels in conjunction with two rules of thumb the blog i linked earlier worked out: a life-long exposure of 33.3 pm2.5 costs 1 daly. this is best for lifestyle changes. for example, moving from somewhere with no particulates to somewhere with a level of 100 costs 3 daly. at 2500 pm2.5, you lose disability-adjusted life in real time.\\\\ this is best for one-off events. for example, if you’re exposed to a level of 5000 for 3 hours, you lose 6 disability-adjusted life hours. using the second rule, we can pretty easily calculate that if you spend 16 hours a day in your dorm, you will lose: (100/2500)\\16 hours/day\\(4\\30 days/semester)\\8 semesters/degree = 614 hours = 25 days in your time at tech. i\'d note that gt housing could easily fix this if they cared to ~~by installing appropriate filtration in their hvac systems~~ (see edit 2), but obviously that won\'t happen. instead, i want to strongly encourage everyone reading this to pick up an air filter, which you can do for less than $100. my friend did this and we confirmed that pm2.5 in their room went down to almost nothing, astonishingly fast. you can keep using it after you graduate; you\'ll probably add months to your life. edit 1: i don\'t use reddit or particularly care if you share this post (actually, i\'d encourage you to share the original blog post with interested friends), but please do tell people you know that they might want to invest in an air filter. friends don\'t let friends develop chronic respiratory diseases. edit 2: points out that installing filtration in the ducts might not be enough to fix indoor air pollution; you need to clean them out. i\'m not an expert on this, and that seems reasonable to me, but my instinct would be that hvac filtration is a good start. first, hvac filtration is the only mechanism i can think of that would be responsible for my apartment having lower-than-ambient levels of air pollution before i started using my filter, so it clearly does something. second, all pm captured by the filter is not being recirculated into the air you breathe, which seems like it could only be a good thing. i\'m updating my belief on this to something like "hvac filtration is necessary but probably not sufficient to address high levels of indoor air polution, depending on where filters are installed." thanks for catching my mistake!', "ca boy (born and raised in san diego, as well as some time near the bay area) who went tech in the late 80's and early 90's. (after writing this, be sure you don't skip 9 through 11. 1-4 and 9 to 11 are probably the most practical bits of info here, while 5-8 are a little more tongue in cheek) 1) as others have pointed out, atlanta gets a very real second-summer in october, be prepared for humid heat in that time frame. loose fitting shirts, loose fitting shorts (maybe loose fitting pants). 2) sometime in october, it gets chilly fast, and by november its \\_cold\\_. think west coast coastal-winter. 3) thick jacket and scarf for december and january. i had never experienced the arctic blast that travels along north avenue like an icy wind-tunnel. it's not as bad as the worst in other places, but it was one of the big shocks of my first year at tech. your face and ears will likely not be used to something like this unless you were from a mountainous part of the west coast. 4) there is a very short period in the spring (april-ish) where the weather will remind you of spring on the west coast. then the humidity and fire-ants arrive. if your'e going to wear open toe shoes, be very aware of fire-ant hills and pathways. 5) when people in atlanta talk about a big rain storm, think about our current atmospheric rivers. they're probably talking about one of the tropical storms or hurricanes whose perimeters can reach up/in to atlanta and cause a little bit of flooding. the atmospheric rivers can be worse, but it's not a casual rain. (atlanta does get more casual rain, but that's not usually what people mean by a big rain \\_storm\\_). don't drive through standing water, make sure you have a rain coat of some kind (not just a warm coat, a rain coat), and a decent umbrella. and some way to protect your laptop from the rain (that wasn't an issue back when i was there, but i could easily see it being one now). 6) 1 week per year, or so, probably in february or march, the city will completely shut down. it doesn't happen every year, but ... it was kinda 50/50 back in the day. why? ... snow. not a fun amount of snow, but an amount that causes anyone who isn't from the midwest to freak out, buy all of the bread milk and eggs (maybe toilet paper) and drive like idiots for a week (because they don't know they're lousy at driving in snow and ice). people i knew who were from the midwest stayed off the roads not because of the snow/ice, but because of the idiots trying to drive on the snow/ice. so, basically, the people most qualified to drive on the snow/ice were exactly the people who were not out there trying to drive in the snow/ice. unless you're from tahoe or something, don't plan to drive that week unless you have to. 7) you will be tempted to get used to drinking sweetened iced tea. don't. it's just sugar water with a bitter flavoring added to it. if you didn't grow up on it, it will ruin your metabolism. 8) find a place that has real bbq (the best one i used to know of went out of business, unfortunately). the downside is that it will ruin you for real bbq when you go home. (there are one or two good bbq places i've encountered since leaving atlanta ... but most of them are lacking in understanding real bbq). 9) if you have long hair, do not let it drip dry. humidity will make it mildew by afternoon. mildewed hair is not a thing you want to have to deal with. blowdrying might be optional on the west coast, but it's not optional in the humid south east, if you have long hair. 10) similarly, do not leave any partially damp fabrics in a bunch or folded in an enclosed space. atlanta isn't as bad as fl in this regard, but things mildew a lot faster over there, so any dampness is a problem. hang towels, spread out as much as you can. do not fold them until they are bone dry. 11) allergies... there are 50 kinds of mold and spores in the air of atlanta. if you have any kind of allergies at all, be sure you stay on top of whatever your treatment for them might be. and in the spring... the pollen is so bad that it's almost like snow-drifts. i'm not even kidding, there are places where the pollen will change color of \\_lakes\\_ or the near-shore ocean, due to pollen in run-off."]

Representative_Docs: ['fellow vegetarian here. i feel like we are blessed 5o be in a time where new understandings of diet have emerged and vegetarianism is becoming increasingly accessible. in terms of my experiences, 1. cooking so so valuable. you save money and you can start simple. if you have a pan, you can always make a run to publix to get a lotta veggies (different colors), pasta, sauce and whip up your "mostly homemade pasta" 2. in terms of protein, tofu has been a valuable asset. i personally am into making curries. an easy way could be to get some veggies, tofu, and thai curry paste (yellow, red, etc) and whip up a beautiful thai curry in minutes. you can enjoy with rice! also, my roommate and i also like to make quesadillas with refried black beans, veggies, taco seasoning, taco sauce, some chilli powders, cheese and its also not as difficult if you put your mind to it the point is that sometimes we gotta get a bit creative and realize that there are options if you actively try them out! 3. in terms of food options if you dont have time to cook or unable to, below are a list of places that could work (according to my experience + vegetarian friends\' experiences). not exahustive by any means: chipotle rreal tacos lucky buddha govindas cafe (they deliver to campus if you join their whatsapp group. very affordable) food terminal mamouns falafel gyro bros sometimes there\'s this place called marrakech express that comes to campus to serve lunch. price point and food really good', 'people complain about the lack of vegan options, but i\'ve long been convinced that tech students are incredibly unwilling to try anything that isn\'t cfa, panda, or twisted taco, and this attitude contributes to the lack of options. [you certainly can\'t say tech hasn\'t tried in the past, they have]( is the model a food truck still around? wouldn\'t surprise me if they\'ve gotten rid of that too. on the topic of prices, i agree that slutty vegan was expensive, but what would "affordable" look like to you? most dedicated vegan/vegetarian places are not cheap, and the only place you\'ll find a complete meal for under $10 is the value menu at mcd\'s/burger king/wendy\'s.', 'yeah but vegan isn’t vegetarian and that’s my point. this post is bitching about not having vegetarian food not vegan food']

Representative_Docs: ['gt print center took my funds. as the title says. but yeah i went to print some stuff (a large amount as it was stuff for a club and in color) the total for the print load was 7$ so a large portion of my print funds. i went to a printer it didn’t work and didn’t take my print funds. so i went to another printer and it didn’t work and took those over 7$ in print funds. i then talked to the gt print center upstairs and was told they would normally reprint the stuff for me for free but every printer in the library was down. so they directed me towards a working printer and i used it. i then contacted the print center a few days later as these funds weren’t refunded. they said they couldn’t and their policy was for me to go to the print center and for them to print the things for me for free (they said this after i explained why that couldn’t happen and the above interaction). they proceeded to tell me multiple times that this was there policy and there was absolutely no way for me to get these print funds back. i am a club leader and use a lot of my printing because of that. but yeah i’m really upset. and maybe i’m over reacting about 7$. but i also feel like i was stolen from and also felt very ignored in my later interactions with the print center. i’m also writing this to warn people. since this is the policy maybe just print one sheet at first so you lose 14 cents if it’s down unlike me. but at this point what do i even do?', 'is canvas down for anyone else?', "print studio conduct and f.a.q hello there jackets! we at the print studio would like to thank you for using our services and we like to answer some common questions students have about the print studio. however, before we get to that we need to acknowledge some issues: please do not leave posters unclaimed for more than 48 hours (including day of printing). they will be discarded. please do not go into the back room without permission. please do not hesitate to ask us for help at the desk especially if its to release your prints. we have several people who have sat and waited over an hour on several occasions waiting on a poster that never started printing. please try to come early. if you have a presentation at in the morning, before we open, it is not the responsibility of the print studio to print your poster after 9:30 or even before we open. thank you in advance. now for some faq: q: do you have glossy paper?/can you laminate this? a: we neither have glossy paper nor the ability to laminate your poster or regular prints unfortunately. q: can you see my poster? a: we cannot. we can only see the poster if you show us the preview beforehand. we only see the price, file name, and the gt username used for the poster. q: how do i make copies/scan my documents? a: there's 2 scanners in the library: one on the ground floor of crosland and another one right next to us at the print studio (its the color printers). you just hit the email button, place your document in the scanner or feeder, type in the email you wish to send it to, and hit send! we unfortunately cannot make copies so you have to scan your document and print it. q: how do i print on tabloid size?/ how do i print on special paper?/ do you have special paper? a: we do not carry any paper other than letter and tabloid size printer paper, so if you wish to print on a different type, you must supply your own. we recommend installing the print drivers to your computer (go to [print.gatech.edu]( and follow those instructions for your device) that way you can say what size and type of paper you want to print on and can send the job straight to the printer. the color printers have a bypass tray located on the left side of the printer that folds out. put your paper in there, tell the printer what type of paper it is, and continue as you would for a normal print afterwards! q: do i need to reserve a computer to print?/ can i just use my computer to print a poster? a: you must use the macs next to the print studio to print a poster."]

Representative_Docs: ["alright folks, instructor from last fall here. debated whether or not to chime in, but the comments here are going way too far. conte is giving you an option for dealing with cheating that few other profs give. here are the 2 institute approved options when it comes to getting caught for cheating: meet with the professor, dont admit to cheating, get reported to osi and defend yourself there, and it goes on your record if you aren't found innocent. the process also takes months and is a whole lot more stressful meet with the professor, admit to cheating, sign a form, and it still gets sent to osi and ends up on your record what conte/2110 is offering you: admit that you cheated and take a zero on the assignment. you sign a form for our records, nothing will be sent on to osi or otherwise prove your innocence and walk away scot-free don't admit and fail to prove your innocence, and go through osi as option 1 above", 'okay, did op follow the procedure to actually introduce those witnesses to the school? did those witnesses see anything occur or did they just notice this guy hanging around at the party? i don’t know. how would i know that? i read what you read. either way the witnesses should have been heard. that goes against your argument that it’s a he said she said. i get that false accusations are a tough situation to deal with. that’s why the witnesses are so important. in a real court, evidence has to be introduced before the actual trial. in this case, the investigator probably would have liked to interview said witnesses before the “trial” in a 1:1 setting to cross reference testimonies. the investigator may have even interviewed them (op didn’t say) and determined they weren’t a credible witness. again, it doesn’t sound like the school did anything wrong, op just wasn’t prepared. we can talk about the failures of the regular court system in the states and how fair it is but i digress. why would op be “prepared” to be raped. do you walk around prepped to be a victim of any crime that happens to you. do you know how to ensure justice is served in all situations? and even if you do, should you have to? there are people in charge of that and they should do their due diligence. yes, a fraternity can and should defend a member who is accused of rape until a higher authority determines the outcome. fraternities are led by a group of college men, and are not qualified to indict someone of a serious crime. if a member is found guilty, and the fraternity does not remove the member, then obviously they are not an organization with morals. if the fraternity chooses to remove a member for unbecoming conduct before a guilty verdict, that is their own choice but should not be mandated. no they shouldn’t. their job isn’t to defend people accused. they can do an investigation because they’re a group of adults. just like any other organization would do. if there’s an accusation of sexual assault or misconduct in a company there is an internal investigation. that should be a normal expectation of adults. you don’t just believe one side or the other. you check first so that your biases don’t end up accusing the innocent or defending a rapist. i didn’t say it should be mandated. i said it’s wrong. i have no control over what fraternities do. i do think they should change a lot especially when they become safe havens for perpetrators of long forms of sexual misconduct.', "this is nonsense - and my engagement is going to end after this response. your numbers don't even make sense... you are telling me that the 58+ other students admitted it? or decided taking the 0 was worth no longer dealing with your abusive process? you, clearly, believe in your tool and there isn't anything i'm going to do to convince you otherwise . neither is the evidence that these don't work and are biased (including, by inference, [against people ]( you]( it makes me sad that you (i would call that a professional failing) or osi would. students shouldn't have (and don't) have to prove their innocence, yet here we are. i'm going to higlight two other comments you made in this thread. 1) i should be clear that i'm not an instructor this semester. that said, copying 1 function is the same level of dishonesty as copying the entire thing. so if you have 1 function with high similarity, you could still get flagged the crass generalization goes from 'any evidence of cheating is cheating' to 'any cheating is the same as all cheating' ipso factor any evidence of cheating is evidence of all cheating is just...wow. just, no. 2) we caught close to 250 flags last fall, almost all of which admitted to cheating. we just choose not to ruin their careers and let them walk away with a 0 instead of an osi record this is actually against gt rules. faculty cannot apply a grade penalty without going through the process. [doing so is against the student code of conduct and the honor code]( they can go through faculty conference resolution, but you should know the difference here if you are dealing with this many cases. i am willing to bet, from experience, that the course didn't do that. it is telling that the more you explain this the less i actually trust anything you are saying. you are detailing a predatory process that there are rules against to protect students. you are relying on the fear that such accusations garner from students to enable and conduct abuses of power. by gt rules, you found 0 students cheating last semester."]

Name: 16_gold_white_wear_yellow
Representative_Docs: ['i don\'t remember ever hearing of us wearing that sort of uniform. certainly not in the modern era, and all the pics i\'ve seen of the pre-dodd years were always (mostly) solid jerseys. per some of the discussion above, dodd also was a fan of white jerseys for home. our colors are "white and gold," not "gold and white," so perhaps that has somethign to do with it. if you\'re interested in the history of tech football, go find a used copy of dodd\'s luck to get an idea of his perspective on his time at tech. it\'s a good read, as is "focused on the top" (about the 1990 national championship season), :dress her in white and gold," and "you dropped it, you pick it up" (about the 222-0 cumberland game - hard to find, and currently runs $400 on most used book sites, but a fun read.) welcome! if you haven\'t learned the words to "up with the white and gold," "i\'m a ramblin\' wreck from georgia tech," and the budweiser song, get to it! btw - it\'s tough to come up with my favorite football uniform combo. while i loved the navy jerseys from the 1990 year, as well as the mustard jerseys from the calvin johnson era, i think the best would be gold/white/gold, followed by white/gold/white. what can i say, i\'m a purist.', 'old gold and white are the official colors. black has been used as accent color as well as navy blue and navy blue is not the official secondary color. “yellow gold” was not an official color even though buzz is yellow.', 'colors have always been white and gold. since gold is metallic, it’s difficult to reproduce in textured surfaces like textiles. various shades of yellow have been used to approximate gold. using an accent color allows you to use gold on parts of the uniform that are easier, e.g. helmet, numbers, piping, and have options other than solid white. the accent color changed from black to navy blue sometime in the 80s, but i don’t know why. the classic home uni to me is white jerseys, gold pants, gold helmet with solid white gt. this keeps the accent color to a minimum. of course baseball and basketball uniforms are all fabric, so again the gold is tough. those uniforms have always been white or relied heavily on the accent color.']

Name: 17_career_company_offer_fair
Representative_Docs: ['is career buzz a career fair?', "alum here. i once worked the gt career fair for a former employer. for the most part, unless you have a formal interview right there and then, you can get away with business casual at a career fair. ​ the people working the fair may or may not be hiring managers with the authority to choose which candidates they want to screen/interview/hire ( i'd say most of the time not). ​ use the career fair to: 1 - collect intelligence on the company, what openings they have, what teams/departments might interest you, or any other aspects that pique your interest (i.e. do they have an office in a geographical location you want to work in, do they do direct work in an industry that you're trying to break into). 2 - get/keep the contact information for the people you speak with. this is networking 101. that person is your in if you decide to apply and want to get information about your prospects, status of application or any other postings that might be forthcoming. if you keep things professional then most employees personable enough to work a career fair will be happy to stay in contact with a desirable candidate. 3 - put on your sales hat. academic accolades and top grades are all good to have, but coming across as friendly, capable, intelligent, competent and motivated makes an equally lasting impression. being able to put a favorably-remembered face to the name on a resume is going to be more helpful than a carefully crafted cover letter. ​ the reason why some people suggest that you target companies is because there isn't enough time in the day (or even two days) to have this type of 3-5 minute conversation with every potential employer. who you choose to spend time and effort on (and why) is your business, but there is value in not spreading yourself so thinly that absolutely none of the people at the 24 companies you speak with remember anything about you. ​ good luck. college career fairs are much happier affairs than career fairs when you're an unemployed adult.", 'interview during career fair? advantage of career fair?']

Representative_Docs: ['job opportunity: real-time visual unity developer - design movement feedback for an ai installation - ($15/hr - fall 2024 + spring 2025) [ksu performance in may 2024]( the [expressive machinery lab]( at georgia tech is seeking a talented undergraduate real-time unity developer with strong graphic design abilities to design real-time visual feedback for an ai-driven installation at the museum of science and industry in chicago for a project titled, [fostering ai literacy through embodiment and creativity across informal learning spaces]( your work will directly engage visitors by classifying and reflecting their movements based on the body action taxonomy (bat) system—an innovative framework developed to interpret and categorize movement patterns. # about the project this opportunity is part of luminai, an interactive ai system where human and machine collaboration occurs through dance and movement. the installation features a three-panel design aimed at promoting ai literacy among middle school students and museum visitors. your visual feedback solutions will enhance the installation\'s immersive quality, providing engaging, real-time interaction for museum-goers. resources: please take a look at our recent public dissemination of luminai in the context of movement improvisation[– a performance at kennesaw state university with dance major students]( we recommend watching a [quick tech overview of the project]( as well as an [overview of the research process]( we conducted over the past year. job focus in this role, you will focus on: 1. designing and implementing real-time visual feedback that reacts to participants\' movements using the body action taxonomy system. 2. collaborating with the team in weekly meetings to coordinate deadlines, refine designs, and implement feedback-driven improvements. this role offers significant responsibility, as you will replace the lab’s previous real-time visual developer. we are looking for a quick learner who is proactive and able to contribute creatively. # (preferred) familiarity with mongodb or other unity-compatible databases for saving user interactions. experience with qa, documentation, and the ability to communicate technical ideas clearly. (bonus) knowledge or experience in dance, movement arts, or embodied interaction. what you’ll gain this role provides hands-on experience at the intersection of ai, motion science, and interactive design, with the chance to see your work implemented in a public-facing installation visited by thousands. it’s an excellent opportunity for students passionate about immersive technologies and ai literacy. application details commitment: 10 hours per week for fall 2024 (october – december) and spring 2025 (january – april). pay: $15/hr (we wish we could pay higher - must adhere to nsf pay guidelines) or class credit apply: send your resume and weekly availability to dr. milka trajkova at [mtrajkova3@gatech.edu](mailto:mtrajkova3@gatech.edu) for immediate hire with subject line: "visual unity developer role" be part of a unique opportunity to shape an innovative installation at one of the world\'s leading science museums!', 'the ai safety initiative invites you to apply to the ai safety fundamentals seminar program by this sunday (9/18)! modern ai has outpaced our ability to explain its behavior, instill our values in its objectives, and build robust safeguards against its failures. yet, companies and governments are spending billions of dollars a year to displace humans as the most intelligent agents on the planet. what if they succeed? Representative_Docs: ['i will give the story as i know it from my second-row seat in his 1371 class. i see very few people actually describing the context in detail. he walked in late or just barely on time like always. he had another class (cs 1331 section c) right before ours (cs 1371 b) so he would always get to ours later. when he set up at his desk, he was surprised to find a fully-wrapped, new (unused) tampon sitting on the desk. landry typically started out his class with some off topic rants or observations before eventually diving into course content. that day, his off topic intro was about the tampon on the desk. he said something along the lines of "there\'s a tampon here. why would that be? who needs one in a classroom and not a bathroom?"
